about: The red-eyed tree frog's walking scan (art-src/raw/redeye_walk_mesh.glb, the owner's, 6 Oct 2026) in the frog pose bake's frame: rotY 128, trunk x centred by 0.274 (job.center), then levelled about x (20.6 deg) as tools/bake-frogpose.mjs analyse() does; scan units (the trunk, snout to vent, is about 1.55 long). Measured with tools/rig/limb-axes.mjs (centrelines by geodesic bands from the vent), the right hind leg partly by eye from close views (it is folded in a tight Z: thigh forward and out, shin back, foot forward). First draft: +-0.05 on a joint; not yet checked against the skin binding.
notes: The head is rolled in the scan: the right eye bump is higher (y top 0.23) than the left (0.11), centroids about (0.17, 0.17, 0.76) and (-0.10, 0.07, 0.76): the trunk itself is not rolled (left and right belly levels agree to 0.02 up to z 0.45). Un-roll the head (the trunk vertices in front of z 0.55, blended over 0.45-0.55, about the z axis, about 20 deg) before the eyes are fitted, or the mirrored eye lands off the left bump.
The two hind legs have different bone lengths in the scan (left thigh 0.45, shin 0.65; right thigh 0.62, shin 0.55): a pose, or the folded right leg misread; check against the skin binding.
